s-16-1-correct.alt: A table, the shot list, with columns Subject, Where, How and Status. Two rows are photographs in the guide, the Capitol Rotunda in 2005 and a public meeting at Lake Isabella in 2014; ten rows are subjects to commission, from a planning board meeting in a school cafeteria to a volunteer with a clipboard on a sidewalk, each with where it is set and how to shoot it.
s-16-1-correct.notes: Live text. Rows 3 to 12 take their subjects from our fifth edition’s shot list (Phase 0 census, photography entries 30 to 49), with a level and a region added; the How lines are the guide’s own direction.

s-16-1-failure.alt: Failure case: do not publish. The upper walls of the Capitol Rotunda in black and white: two large framed paintings between carved stone panels and pilasters, and no people.

s-16-10-correct.alt: A storyboard of six video frames with their times and words: the title frame with the question at 0:00; Dustin on camera with his name plate at 0:02; at 0:08 and 0:30, chart S04 with its source line under it and the captions on a Charcoal band, the 0:30 captions saying the gap grew from 23 points to 27; the step at 0:50; the end frame at 1:00.
s-16-10-correct.notes: The video is not made, so the plate carries the Illustrative label at its head; every figure is chart S04’s (work/build/chart-kit/specs/s04.json). The 0:08 and 0:30 cells are the application kit’s A21 frames at 1920 by 1080 (views 1920-light-chart and 1920-light-gap), shown at 10 percent. The step frame holds the view’s one working red.

s-16-10-failure.alt: Failure case: do not publish. The same storyboard with the logo animating to music at 0:00, a greeting at 0:08 and the question only at 0:21.

s-16-11-correct.alt: A vertical video frame at a quarter of 1080 by 1920, for a platform that takes no caption file and draws no captions of its own: chart S04 near the top, the L8 monogram at the top right, and under the chart a Charcoal band that holds the chart’s source line and two caption lines burned into the picture, Citizens 18 to 24 reported voting at 47.7 percent, down 3.7 points. The safe areas show when the page loads, and a switch hides them. A dashed outline runs 269 px in from the top, 120 px from each side and 672 px from the bottom, from TikTok’s and Instagram’s ad guides, and a hatched box marks TikTok’s button column at the right. Beside the frame, the checked WebVTT file the captions come from, with these two lines, the next two and their times.
s-16-11-correct.notes: The application kit’s A21 frame, 1080 by 1920 (view 1080-light), shown at a quarter: chart S04 from the chart kit, its source line and the caption band inside the vertical safe area (DD12b-R1). The frame is a picture whose alt carries every word (D4-211). The video is not made.

s-16-11-failure.alt: Failure case: do not publish. The same frame, where the automatic captions read Citizens 18 to 24 reported voting at 47.7 percent, down 37 points.
s-16-11-failure.notes: The same A21 frame with the automatic caption (view 1080-light-misheard), so the caption is the one fault.

s-16-12-correct.alt: A two-column script, On screen and Said, three rows that read chart S04’s figures and source aloud, then a transcript excerpt with the speaker, the time, the words and a bracketed line for what is on screen, and a link to the chart’s table.
s-16-12-correct.notes: The link goes to chart S04’s rule in chapter 14, where its table opens.

s-16-12-failure.alt: Failure case: do not publish. The same script with one row: the chart on screen, and the voice saying As you can see, young people dropped off right here.

s-16-13-correct.alt: A video card: a Charcoal poster with the question Which age groups reported voting in 2024? and L8 at its corner; under it the title, the length 1:05, a one-sentence finding, a Play button and the links Read the transcript and Watch on YouTube.
s-16-13-correct.notes: Controls drawn as text, since nothing can load in the guide; L8 from its master, 48 px wide, 24 px in from the poster’s top and right edges (Rule 12.3).

s-16-13-failure.alt: Failure case: do not publish. An empty dark box at video size with the words Video unavailable in small gray type, and nothing else.
s-16-13-failure.notes: Picture of a fault: Stone words on Charcoal, 3.10 to 1, as the empty player it copies.

s-16-2-correct.alt: Two panels. The Capitol Rotunda photograph in black and white with its caption, and beside it a placeholder frame for a photograph kept in color: a resident holding up a jar of brown tap water at a city council hearing, whose caption names the color as the evidence.

s-16-2-failure.alt: Failure case: do not publish. The Lake Isabella meeting photograph with a Prussian duotone: dark blue shadows and pale highlights over the official, the residents and the map.
s-16-2-failure.notes: Picture of a fault: a Prussian duotone, drawn by two blended layers over the black and white photograph (screen in Prussian, then multiply in Newsprint). No red on the plate.

s-16-3-correct.alt: The Lake Isabella photograph four times in black and white, each labeled with its ratio and use: 3:2 for articles and reports, 16:9 for a video poster, 1:1 for a square post and 4:5 for a portrait post. Each keeps the official explaining and at least one resident.
s-16-3-correct.notes: CSS crops: 3:2 at 50% 50%, 16:9 at 50% 20%, 1:1 at 25% 50%, 4:5 at 35% 50% (the plan’s rectangles).

s-16-3-failure.alt: Failure case: do not publish. A 4:5 crop of the Lake Isabella photograph: one resident seen from behind and the project map, with the official cut out, over the caption that names him.

s-16-4-correct.alt: An article opener: the kicker Report, Public lands, then the headline as live text, then the Lake Isabella photograph in black and white and its caption.
s-16-4-correct.notes: The kicker opens with one content label, Report (Rule 01.21); the headline is live text in the H3 style.

s-16-4-failure.alt: Failure case: do not publish. The same headline in pale type set straight across the photograph, over the residents and the map, with a soft shadow; parts of it fade into the map, down to 1.0 to 1.
s-16-4-failure.notes: Picture of a fault: Newsprint words on the photograph. Measured by this generator: the ground under the headline’s box falls to 1.0 to 1 against Newsprint, and 17 percent of it is under 3 to 1.

s-16-5-correct.alt: The Rotunda photograph small in black and white, beside its caption with each part underlined and keyed: who, what, who, what, where, when and the credit, with a note that the record dates the photograph only to two days.
s-16-5-correct.notes: Each part’s key comes first in reading order and shows under its words (column-reverse).

s-16-5-failure.alt: Failure case: do not publish. The Lake Isabella photograph in black and white over an invented caption: angry homeowners confront an Army official over the seizure of their land.

s-16-6-correct.alt: The Lake Isabella photograph in black and white with two numbered markers: 1 beside the official, 2 on a resident’s back. A key says the official is named with his role and the residents are unnamed. Under it, the rights record: maker, agency, date, place, license, consent and rights rows.
s-16-6-correct.notes: Markers set in HTML over the frame (contract C1), hidden from a screen reader; the key carries their words.

s-16-6-failure.alt: Failure case: do not publish. A placeholder frame for a close portrait of a ninth grader speaking at a school board meeting, with an invented caption that names her, her age and her school, and a record line that shows no permission from a parent or guardian.

s-16-7-correct.alt: Two crops of the Rotunda photograph in black and white, each with its alt text printed under it: the wide crop’s mentions the casket, the tight crop’s mentions the line of mourners, a wreath and a painting.
s-16-7-correct.notes: Each printed alt text is the same words as its alt.

s-16-7-failure.alt: Failure case: do not publish. The tight crop of the Rotunda photograph, with the wide crop’s alt text printed under it, which names a casket the crop does not show.

s-16-8-correct.alt: Two placeholder frames with corner crop marks and no fill. On Newsprint, a 3:2 frame: Placeholder, photograph to commission, a resident testifies at a microphone in a state house hearing room. On Charcoal, a 4:5 frame with the same words in Charcoal’s colors.
s-16-8-correct.notes: The 4:5 frame stacks its metadata one part a line (CR-14).

s-16-8-failure.alt: Failure case: do not publish. A Stone panel at a photograph’s size with a small caption bar reading A polling place in a gymnasium and Natural color 3:2, which our fifth edition announced to screen readers as a photograph.
s-16-8-failure.notes: Our fifth edition’s panel, redrawn as a picture: an image stage, so the guide’s own reader hears its alt.

s-16-9-correct.alt: A placeholder frame for a generated image, with the Generated image tab at its top left and the written prompt inside: a phone on a kitchen table beside a utility bill and a mug. Under it, a caption that labels the scene as a generated image, with fields for the tool and the date, and a rights record line.
s-16-9-correct.notes: No generated image: the studio’s call for chat 10. The tab sits where it sits on a real one.

s-16-9-failure.alt: Failure case: do not publish. A placeholder frame for a generated picture of a packed hearing room, with no tab, over a news caption and a photograph’s credit for an invented hearing.

s-16-opener.alt: Two documentary photographs in black and white. A federal official answers residents at a public meeting in Lake Isabella, California, in 2014, and members of the public file past the casket of Rosa Parks in the Capitol Rotunda in 2005. Each carries its full caption.
s-16-opener.notes: Both photographs from contract C1, in black and white (Rule 16.2): Lake Isabella by CSS at 3:2, the Rotunda by data-oa-crop 60 0 1080 720, which keeps the agency’s corner mark out.

s-16-picture-kinds.alt: A table of five kinds of picture: documentary photograph, placeholder, hand-drawn spot illustration, exploded view and generated image, with where each may appear, its label, what it never does and its rules.
